title: GTKConfig real isolated export and KDE palette notification

method.isolation: Bubblewrap read-only root; separate PID and network namespaces; private HOME/XDG/runtime/tempia-backed /tmp; private session D-Bus; unavailable system D-Bus; only gtkconfig.so mounted in the KDED module directory.
method.fixture: Private kdeglobals contained the effective DomainOS color-role groups and selected LookAndFeelPackage. The test then changed General/ColorScheme and Colors:Window/BackgroundNormal and emitted the same org.kde.kconfig.notify.ConfigChanged signal used by the production bridge.

result.loaded_modules_introspection: An optional diagnostic queried an unsupported interface at /modules; it was not used as evidence. The mounted KDED plugin directory contained only gtkconfig.so.

limits: This proves the installed GTKConfig module exports effective KDE color roles after the native KConfig notification in a constrained private KDED process.
It does not yet prove the production theme companion watcher and GTK2 palette runtime in the same process chain; R121 separately covers the watcher/QProcess/reload using a private GTKConfig fixture.

The first fixture attempt supplied only a ColorScheme filename and correctly fell back to Breeze defaults. The passing run included the effective Colors:* groups in private kdeglobals, matching the roles consumed by KColorScheme.

The private run logged non-fatal GLib file-monitor and KConfig update warnings; GTKConfig returned the selected theme and both color exports changed as expected. No host theme, XSettings process, color scheme, or user window was altered.
next: Combine the real isolated GTKConfig module with the already-tested production theme_companion_bridge observer and GTK2 2.24 runtime in one private test, then resume remaining GtkEntry/VM and visual gaps. Keep XChat and the personal GTK profile unchanged until I167 is actually closed.
